- ep_7d9234: lme_5 recently learned to use a slow cooker and made a beef stew, then asked for more slow cooker recipe ideas. The assistant suggested recipes across classic, global, vegetarian/vegan and comfort-food categories. lme_5 then asked about making yogurt in a slow cooker. The assistant gave a basic method: heat milk to 180-185F, cool to 110-120F, stir in a live-culture yogurt starter, incubate 8-12 hours wrapped in a towel, then chill. It explained why a thermometer is recommended over timing alone. Because lme_5 wants to eat more plant-based meals, lme_5 asked for vegetarian and vegan slow cooker recipes and for vegan yogurt bases; the assistant listed soy, coconut, almond, cashew, oat, rice, hemp and flax options. lme_5 also asked about flavorings and sweeteners (vanilla, cinnamon, honey, maple syrup, monk fruit, stevia, fruit, granola, nuts) and then said lme_5 wants to try a cashew-based slow cooker yogurt. The assistant explained how to soak cashews (at least 4 hours, changing the water), blend them with about 1/2 cup water for roughly 2 minutes, strain them (cheesecloth, nut milk bag or fine sieve), and adjust thickness. lme_5 asked the cashew soaking and blending question twice, and the assistant gave a shorter restatement the second time. The window does not show whether lme_5 has made the yogurt yet.

- ep_2a7564: lme_5 said they had been relying heavily on food delivery and wanted to return to cooking at home. At the time of the 2023-05-26 conversation, it had been about three weeks since their last scratch-cooked meal. The assistant suggested quick, healthy, international and meal-prep ideas. lme_5 chose one-pot pasta and lentil soup and asked for versions using bell peppers and onions already at home; the assistant gave full recipes. lme_5 then planned weekly meal prep and asked how to portion the dishes, which the assistant answered with 5-6 portions, reheating to 165°F, and storage of 5 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer. lme_5 also asked how to balance protein, vegetables and carbs and keep the week varied; the assistant gave protein and vegetable options and a sample weekly plan. lme_5 next asked for airtight, leak-resistant containers for on-the-go use, and the assistant listed glass, plastic, stainless steel, collapsible and bento options. Last, lme_5 asked for stir-fry tips, and the assistant covered pan choice, high heat, batch cooking, aromatics first, high-smoke-point oil and adding sauces last. lme_5 said they would try the recipes. No results are recorded.

- ep_71d15a: lme_5 asked for vegan recipes, specifically a vegan quiche, and mentioned a vegan spot downtown whose vegan mac and cheese lme_5 first tried two weeks before the conversation and now eats often as comfort food. The assistant suggested five vegan quiche recipes and general quiche tips. lme_5 said lme_5 will try the Tofu and Spinach Quiche first and asked whether oat milk would work, which lme_5 has been enjoying. The assistant said oat milk is workable but slightly sweet, and listed soy, almond, cashew and rice milk alternatives. lme_5 also plans to host a vegan dinner party and asked for vegan lasagna tips. The assistant gave layering, pasta, sauce, ricotta, filling and resting advice, and recommended a Mushroom and Spinach Lasagna with Cashew Ricotta. lme_5 said lme_5 will make that lasagna and described the cashew-based cheese sauce at the downtown mac and cheese spot, which is still on lme_5's mind. The assistant encouraged trying a cashew mac and cheese at home. lme_5 then asked how to store leftover lasagna, and the assistant gave cooling, refrigeration, freezing, labelling and reheating guidance. lme_5 also says coconut-based yogurt is lme_5's favorite vegan yogurt, and asked how to use it in recipes instead of traditional yogurt. The assistant suggested 1:1 substitution, baking, savory dishes, marinades, Indian dishes and thickening uses, along with brands such as So Delicious, Kite Hill and Coconut Bliss.
